rows.d: o = flop q (1) or combinational (0)
rows.n: Chooses whether the block is registered. The single most common bit to change: clear for a gate, set for state.

rows.d: value loaded into q on synchronous reset
rows.n: Makes the flop an FDRE (0) or an FDSE (1). Only consulted when FF_SR_EN is set and sr is high.

rows.d: 1 = flop honours ce, 0 = always enabled
rows.n: With this clear the flop follows comb on every TCK. Set it and the flop only moves on an explicit enable, which is how a scan chain single-steps logic.

rows.d: 1 = flop honours sr, 0 = reset ignored
rows.n: Lets a block opt out of the global reset. A pipeline stage that must not be cleared leaves this at 0.

rows.d: 1 = carry chain drives the datapath
rows.n: Re-purposes the LUT: o6 stops being the answer and becomes the propagate term. The datapath takes o6 XOR cin.
Where the carry generate term comes from. Using o5 is what lets one block do add, subtract and compare with the fracture.
Selects the fractured output as the registered value. Ignored when CY_EN is set.
